title: Peace and petitions
summary: After peace is established between the people of Lehi and Morianton over their lands, contention arises over Pahoran and proposed changes to the law. Pahoran refuses to alter it or heed the petitions.
characters: petitioners seeking changes to the law

explicit_facts.text: Peace was established between the people of Lehi and the people of Morianton concerning their lands.
Contention arose concerning Pahoran, as some people wanted particular points of the law altered.
Pahoran would not alter the law or heed the petitions concerning its alteration.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown presenting petitions to Pahoran.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Pahoran and the petitioners; the exact place where the petitions were presented.

narration.text: they did not long maintain an entire peace in the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not supply the petitioners’ words or any dialogue.

title: The division over Pahoran
summary: Those who want the law changed grow angry and want Pahoran removed. The two sides become known as king-men and freemen, with the freemen covenanted to maintain their rights and religious privileges through free government.

explicit_facts.text: Those wanting changes were angry with Pahoran and wanted him no longer to be chief judge; the dispute did not reach bloodshed.
Those seeking Pahoran’s removal were called king-men and wanted a king established over the land.
Those wanting Pahoran to remain chief judge took the name freemen and had covenanted to maintain their rights and religious privileges by free government.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two factions may be shown in a tense, nonviolent dispute.
unspecified_visual_details: Faction clothing, symbols, and the precise venue of the dispute.

narration.text: there arose a warm dispute concerning the matter, but not unto bloodshed

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray violence in this dispute.

title: The people choose the freemen
summary: The people’s voice favors the freemen, and Pahoran retains the judgment-seat. His supporters rejoice; the king-men are silenced and obliged to maintain the cause of freedom. The narration notes that supporters of kings sought power and authority.

explicit_facts.text: The people’s voice favored the freemen; Pahoran retained the judgment-seat, and many rejoiced.
The king-men were put to silence and obliged to maintain the cause of freedom.
Those in favor of kings were of high birth and sought power and authority over the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Supporters may be shown rejoicing after the decision.
unspecified_visual_details: How the people expressed their voice, and the setting and appearance of the gathering.

narration.text: the voice of the people came in favor of the freemen

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a formal voting procedure or a public speech.

title: Amalickiah prepares for war
summary: While contention divides the Nephites, Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites against them, gathers and arms soldiers, and prepares his army to attack. Though smaller than before, the army is still great, and he fears not to descend toward Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah stirred the Lamanites against the Nephites, gathered and armed soldiers, and prepared for war.
Amalickiah prepared himself and his armies to battle against the Nephites.
His army was smaller than before but still great, and he feared not to come down to Zarahemla.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Soldiers may be shown being assembled and armed.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise mustering ground, military equipment, and Amalickiah’s appearance.

narration.text: he was gathering together soldiers from all parts of his land

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Amalickiah’s vow concerning Moroni is reported narration, not a depicted encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Moroni present or invent words spoken by Amalickiah.

title: The Lamanite army descends
summary: Amalickiah himself leads the Lamanites down as Nephite affairs concerning Pahoran are being settled. Hearing that the Lamanites are coming, the king-men refuse to take up arms to defend their country.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah personally came down at the head of the Lamanites during the twenty-fifth year.
The king-men heard that the Lamanites were coming and refused to take up arms to defend their country.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The approaching Lamanite force and the king-men’s refusal may be shown as separate visual elements in this moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place where the king-men receive the news and the appearance of the army.

narration.text: they refused to take up arms

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a messenger or invent how the king-men learned the news.

title: Moroni petitions the governor
summary: Moroni sees the Lamanites coming into the borders of the land and is angered by the stubbornness of people he had labored to preserve. He sends a petition, with the voice of the people, asking the governor for power to compel the dissenters to defend their country or put them to death. The request is granted according to the voice of the people.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni saw the Lamanites coming into the borders of the land and was exceedingly angry at the stubbornness of people he had labored to preserve.
Moroni sent a petition, with the voice of the people, to the governor, seeking power to compel the dissenters to defend their country or put them to death.
The request was granted according to the voice of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown sending the petition, without depicting a face-to-face meeting with the governor.
unspecified_visual_details: The petition’s physical form and means of delivery.
The appearances of Moroni, the dissenters, and the governor.

narration.text: he sent a petition, with the voice of the people, unto the governor of the land,
desiring that he should read it, and give him (Moroni) power to compel those dissenters to defend their country or to put them to death.
And it came to pass that it was granted according to the voice of the people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not name who granted the request.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the dissenters as king-men from these supplied verses.
Do not depict an execution or treat the requested penalty as an event that occurred.
Do not portray Moroni and the governor meeting in person.

title: Moroni marches against the king-men
summary: Moroni orders his army against the king-men, requiring them to take up arms for liberty. When dissenters raise weapons to fight Moroni’s men, they are struck down. Four thousand are slain; surviving leaders are imprisoned without trial at this time.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni commanded his army to go against the king-men, who were to take up arms and support liberty or be brought down.
The armies marched against the king-men; those who raised weapons to fight were hewn down.
Four thousand dissenters were slain, and surviving leaders were taken and imprisoned without trials at that period.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The armed clash may be depicted without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise battlefield and the appearance of the combatants.

narration.text: the armies did march forth against them

prohibited_inventions: Do not show wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: The remainder yield
summary: The remaining dissenters yield to the standard of liberty and are compelled to hoist the title of liberty upon their towers and in their cities, and to take up arms in defense of their country.

explicit_facts.text: The remaining dissenters yielded to the standard of liberty rather than be struck down by the sword.
They were compelled to hoist the title of liberty upon their towers and in their cities, and to take up arms in defense of their country.
Moroni put an end to those known as king-men; they were brought to humble themselves and fight for freedom from bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The title of liberty may be shown raised on a tower.
The dissenters may be shown taking up arms without depicting combat.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the standard and title of liberty.
The towers, cities, and arms' designs.

narration.text: yielded to the standard of liberty,
And thus Moroni put an end to those king-men,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 21 describes the outcome; do not depict the later fighting as simultaneous with the yielding.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent lettering or a design for the title of liberty.
Do not add a battle, wounds, speeches, or an army to this scene.

title: Amalickiah takes the city of Moroni
summary: While Moroni works to end contention among his people and prepare for war, the Lamanites come into the land of Moroni by the seashore. The Nephites in the city of Moroni are not sufficiently strong. Amalickiah drives them, slaying many, and takes possession of the city and all its fortifications.
characters: Nephites in the city of Moroni

explicit_facts.text: Moroni was breaking down wars and contentions among his own people, subjecting them to peace and civilization, and making regulations to prepare for war against the Lamanites.
The Lamanites came into the land of Moroni, which was on the borders by the seashore.
The Nephites were not sufficiently strong in the city of Moroni.
Amalickiah drove the Nephites, slaying many, and took possession of the city and all its fortifications.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites can be shown entering the land by the seashore.
The Nephites can be shown being driven from the city during combat, without showing injuries or gore.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the city and its fortifications.

Amalickiah did drive them, slaying many.
Amalickiah took possession of the city, yea, possession of all their fortifications.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni at the city.

title: Refugees gather at Nephihah
summary: Those who flee Moroni reach Nephihah, while the people of Lehi gather and prepare to receive the Lamanites in battle. Amalickiah does not let the Lamanites attack Nephihah; he keeps them by the seashore and leaves men in each city to defend it.

people of the city of Lehi

explicit_facts.text: Those fleeing Moroni came to Nephihah; the people of Lehi gathered and prepared for battle.
Amalickiah did not allow an attack on Nephihah, kept the Lamanites by the seashore, and left men in every city to defend it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Refugees may be shown arriving at Nephihah while defenders prepare at Lehi.
unspecified_visual_details: The route taken by the refugees and the precise arrangement of defenses.

prohibited_inventions: Do not combine the separate cities into one location.

title: The Lamanites take the eastern cities
summary: Amalickiah’s forces take Nephihah, Lehi, Morianton, Omner, Gid, and Mulek, all on the eastern seashore borders. The many cities are strongly fortified after the manner of Moroni’s fortifications and become Lamanite strongholds.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites took possession of Nephihah, Lehi, Morianton, Omner, Gid, and Mulek, all on the east borders by the seashore.
The cities were strongly fortified after the manner of Moroni’s fortifications and afforded strongholds for the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Fortified walls and occupied cities may be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact appearance of the cities, their walls, and the order in which they were taken.

narration.text: all of which afforded strongholds for the Lamanites

prohibited_inventions: Do not stage all six captures as a single simultaneous event.

title: The Lamanites advance toward Bountiful
summary: The Lamanites march toward Bountiful, driving Nephites before them and slaying many. Teancum meets them; he has slain Morianton and led Morianton’s people in their flight. Teancum also heads off Amalickiah’s advance toward Bountiful and the land northward.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites marched to the borders of Bountiful, driving Nephites before them and slaying many.
Teancum met them after slaying Morianton and leading Morianton’s people in their flight.
Teancum headed Amalickiah off as he marched to take Bountiful and the land northward.

unspecified_visual_details: The precise location of the encounter and the appearance of Morianton’s fleeing people.

title: Teancum repulses Amalickiah’s army
summary: Teancum and his men repulse Amalickiah’s army and gain advantage. They harass the Lamanites until dark. Teancum’s men camp at Bountiful’s borders, while Amalickiah camps on the beach by the seashore.

title: Teancum enters Amalickiah’s camp
summary: At night, Teancum and his servant steal into Amalickiah’s camp. Teancum enters the king’s tent and puts a javelin to Amalickiah’s heart, killing him without waking the servants.

explicit_facts.text: At night, Teancum and his servant went secretly into Amalickiah’s camp while fatigue had overcome the sleepers.

title: Teancum returns to his camp
summary: Teancum returns secretly to his own camp, wakes his sleeping men, and tells them what he has done. He has his army stand ready in case the Lamanites awaken and attack. The twenty-fifth year and Amalickiah’s days end.
